userJob: Set text and interface colours that a person can actually read
problem: A palette taken from the subject's materials clears contrast against some of its own values and not others, and the failure lands on body copy where it costs the most
worksWhen: Every build, at the moment a colour is assigned to text rather than when the palette is chosen
avoidWhen: Never; the numbers are a floor and the palette bends to them, not the other way around
mechanism: color-contrast - Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text (large text 3:1); Material Design
risks: Measuring the palette once in light mode and assuming dark mode inherits the result
Placing a paragraph in the one saturated colour of the palette, which usually clears some grounds and not others
mobileRules: Measure at the sizes actually used at 375px, since a size that counts as large text on desktop may not be large on mobile
accessibilityRules: Body text 4.5:1, large text and interface components 3:1
Measure in both colour schemes, independently, rather than inferring one from the other
genericnessNote: A contrast floor constrains values, not hues, so it can be met in any visual language.

userJob: Size controls so they can be hit on a phone
problem: Icon-only controls get sized to the icon, so the tap area is the glyph and every near miss becomes a mis-tap on a neighbouring control
worksWhen: Every interactive element on any surface that can be reached by touch, which is all of them
avoidWhen: Never; where the visual mark must stay small, the hit area is extended beyond it instead
mechanism: touch-target-size - Min 44×44pt (Apple) / 48×48dp (Material); extend hit area beyond visual bounds if needed
risks: Extending the hit area so far that adjacent targets overlap invisibly
Meeting the size on the button while the real target is an inner span
mobileRules: Keep primary targets away from the screen edges and the gesture bar
accessibilityRules: The enlarged hit area is part of the focusable element, so keyboard focus outlines the real target
An icon-only control carries an accessible name, since the icon is not one
genericnessNote: A minimum size constrains geometry, not style.

userJob: Label a form field so the label is still there while the field is being used
problem: Placeholder text is used as the label, so the moment the user starts typing they lose the name of the thing they are typing into
worksWhen: Any form, on any surface, including single-field forms such as search and newsletter signup
avoidWhen: Never as a design decision; a genuinely label-free field needs an accessible name supplied another way and a visible one nearby
mechanism: input-labels - Visible label per input (not placeholder-only)
risks: A floating label that shrinks into the border on focus becomes decoration at small sizes
Treating the field's surrounding heading as the label, which breaks when the field is reached directly
mobileRules: 16px minimum on inputs, or the browser zooms on focus and the layout jumps
Label above the input rather than beside it, since beside costs the field its width at 375px
accessibilityRules: Use a label element with a for attribute bound to the input id
Placeholder text is a hint, never a name; a hint that vanishes on focus is not a label
genericnessNote: Requiring a visible label leaves its position, weight and voice entirely open.

userJob: Show a validation error where the person can act on it
problem: Errors are collected at the top of the form, so a user on a long form is told something is wrong and has to hunt for which field
worksWhen: Any form with validation, including inline search filters and single-field flows
avoidWhen: Never on its own; a summary at the top is an addition to field-level errors, not a replacement
mechanism: error-placement - Show error below the related field
risks: The error text pushes the layout down, so the field the user was looking at moves
Colour-only error states, which vanish for a reader who cannot separate the hues
mobileRules: Reserve the error line's height so the field does not jump when validation runs
Keep the error visible when the on-screen keyboard is open
accessibilityRules: Bind the error text to the field so it is announced with the field, and mark the field invalid
For multiple errors, add a summary at the top with links to each field, reachable first by keyboard
Error text meets 4.5:1 against the section background
genericnessNote: Placement relative to the field is a structural rule with no visual signature.

userJob: Return the user to the problem after a failed submit
problem: Submit fails, the page re-renders, and focus is at the top of the document, so a keyboard or screen reader user has to walk the whole form again to find what failed
worksWhen: Any form that can fail validation on submit
avoidWhen: Never; even a single-field form benefits, because focus otherwise lands on the document body
mechanism: focus-management - After submit error, auto-focus the first invalid field (WCAG, MD)
risks: Moving focus while the user is still typing, which fights the person rather than helping them
Focusing a field that is scrolled out of view without scrolling it into view
mobileRules: Focusing a field opens the keyboard, so scroll the field clear of the keyboard as part of the move
accessibilityRules: Announce the failure through a live region as well as moving focus
For several errors, focus the summary and link each entry to its field
genericnessNote: Focus behaviour is invisible and cannot contribute to visual sameness.

userJob: Decide when to tell someone their input is wrong
problem: Validating on every keystroke marks a field invalid while it is still being filled, so the user is corrected before they have finished the word
worksWhen: Text entry with a format the user cannot see in advance: email, postcode, card number, phone
avoidWhen: A field with live constraints the user asked for, such as a password strength meter or an availability check they triggered
mechanism: inline-validation - Validate on blur (not keystroke); show error only after user finishes input (MD)
risks: Blur validation fires when the user tabs away to check something, which reads as a rebuke
Never validating until submit, which is the opposite failure and costs a round trip
mobileRules: Blur on mobile can be triggered by dismissing the keyboard, so do not treat blur as abandonment
accessibilityRules: Once a field is marked invalid, re-validate as it changes so the message clears without another blur
Errors are announced politely rather than interrupting
genericnessNote: Validation timing is behaviour, not appearance.

userJob: Convey state without depending on a reader separating two hues
problem: Stock, status and validity are shown as a coloured dot or a coloured row, so a reader who cannot separate the hues gets no information at all
worksWhen: Everywhere state is shown: stock levels, run status, validity, availability, chart series
avoidWhen: Never; colour may carry the state as well, but never alone
mechanism: color-not-only - Don't convey info by color alone (add icon/text)
risks: Adding an icon that is itself only distinguishable by colour
Adding a text label so small it fails contrast, which restores the original problem
mobileRules: At 375px the text carrier is often dropped for space, which silently reintroduces colour-only state; drop something else
accessibilityRules: Pair every signal colour with a word, a shape or a position
In charts, supplement colour with pattern, texture or direct labels
genericnessNote: The rule adds a carrier and does not name which one, so the answer differs per subject.

userJob: Make an animated page usable for someone who has asked for less motion
problem: The preference is honoured by shortening durations, so the movement is still there and the page still triggers the symptom the setting exists to prevent
worksWhen: Any page with transitions, scroll effects, parallax, autoplay or staged reveals
avoidWhen: Never; a page with no motion satisfies it trivially
mechanism: reduced-motion - Respect prefers-reduced-motion; reduce/disable animations when requested (Apple Reduced Motion API, MD)
risks: Stopping only the visible animation while the scroll listener, timer or video keeps running
Reduced motion hiding content that only appeared through the animation
mobileRules: The preference is set at the operating system level and applies at every width; do not gate the media query on a breakpoint
accessibilityRules: Under the preference the work stops, not merely the visible movement
Content revealed by animation is present and readable without the animation
genericnessNote: A motion preference constrains behaviour under a condition and leaves the default composition free.

userJob: Keep a page inside the width of a small phone
problem: One element with a fixed width, an unbroken string or a negative margin pushes the document wider than the viewport, and every section then scrolls sideways
worksWhen: Every build, checked at 320px rather than at 375px
avoidWhen: A region that is deliberately a horizontal scroller, which scrolls inside its own container and never the document
mechanism: horizontal-scroll - No horizontal scroll on mobile; ensure content fits viewport width
risks: Hiding the symptom with overflow-x hidden on the body, which clips content instead of fixing the width
Wide tables and code blocks scrolling the page rather than themselves
mobileRules: Wide content scrolls inside its own container with an overflow rule of its own
accessibilityRules: A horizontally scrolling region is reachable and scrollable by keyboard
Content must not require two-dimensional scrolling to read a single line
genericnessNote: A width constraint says nothing about what fills the width.

userJob: Let a reader enlarge the page
problem: The viewport tag is copied from a template that disables user scaling, so anyone who needs larger text cannot get it and no error is reported anywhere
worksWhen: Every page, set once in the document head
avoidWhen: Never; there is no design reason that outranks a reader's ability to zoom
risks: maximum-scale or user-scalable=no copied in from a legacy starter
A layout that technically allows zoom but breaks into overlap at 200 percent
mobileRules: Check the layout at 200 percent zoom at 375px, not only at the default scale
16px on inputs so the browser does not zoom on focus by itself
accessibilityRules: Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function
genericnessNote: A viewport declaration has no visual expression at all.

userJob: Set numbers that sit in a column, a price, or a running total
problem: Proportional figures make each digit a different width, so a column of prices does not align and a live total shifts sideways as it updates
worksWhen: Prices, quantities, timers, measured values, any figure that repeats down a column or updates in place
avoidWhen: A single display number used as an image, where the proportional cut is usually the better drawing
mechanism: number-tabular - Use tabular/monospaced figures for data columns, prices, and timers to prevent layout shift
risks: Enabling tabular figures on a face that does not have them, which silently does nothing
Applying it to all body text, which makes running prose look like a receipt
mobileRules: A shifting total is more disruptive at 375px, where the figure is often near the acquire control
accessibilityRules: Alignment is a reading aid, not a substitute for a header; the column still needs a label
genericnessNote: Tabular figures are a typographic setting available in many faces, so it constrains rendering rather than choice of face.

userJob: Render a listing of many rows without the screen becoming unusable
problem: A shift's worth of rows is rendered in full, so scrolling stutters, memory climbs, and the operator's own filters become slow to apply
worksWhen: Lists whose length is driven by data rather than by the design, typically past a few dozen rows
avoidWhen: A short, fixed list, where virtualisation adds a scroll container, a measurement pass and a class of bugs for nothing
mechanism: virtualize-lists - Virtualize lists with 50+ items to improve memory efficiency and scroll performance
risks: Browser find-in-page stops working, because the rows the user is searching for are not in the document
Anchor links and restore-scroll behaviour break when the target row is unmounted
mobileRules: Row height estimation errors compound faster on a short viewport, so measure rather than assume
Keep momentum scrolling smooth; a virtualiser that renders on every scroll event will not
accessibilityRules: Expose the total row count so a screen reader user is not told the list is as long as the rendered window
Keyboard traversal reaches rows outside the rendered window, which means the container manages focus
genericnessNote: Virtualisation is an implementation technique with no visual signature.
